references.text: The second commandment forbids making carved images or any representation. This is the foundational commandment that Exodus 34:17 repeats, focusing on cast idols.
The same prohibition against cast idols is repeated in the Holiness Code, with a reminder that the Lord is your God.
A curse is pronounced upon anyone who makes carved or cast images, underscoring the seriousness of the commandment.
The golden calf that Aaron made is an example of breaking this commandment—a cast god made of gold.
Jeroboam made cast calves of gold, a direct violation of the prohibition against cast idols.
Isaiah warns that those who trust in cast images and call them their gods will be put to shame.
Hosea condemns Israel for making cast images of silver, an act of idolatry that led to their downfall.
Paul urges the Athenians that the divine should not be compared to images made by human art and thought.
An expanded formulation of the prohibition against making gods in silver and gold as a direct consequence of God's exclusivity.
A retelling of Mosaic law that extends the prohibition from cast images to all forms of human or animal representations.
A restatement of the second commandment with an identical definition of forbidden representations throughout all creation.
Prophetic confirmation that human-made idols are empty, providing a theological basis for the law's prohibition.
